West Bengal weather IMD alert! Heavy rains on Oct 28, 29, 30 — List of regions, areas, districts to be hit due to storm
The cyclone is likely to make landfall near Andhra Pradesh on October 28, triggering extremely heavy rainfall in parts of Odisha, West Bengal and other states.
Several states, including Odisha, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and West Bengal, are bracing for heavy rainfall this week as preparations are underway to deal with the potential impact of Cyclone Arnab.
The cyclone is likely to make landfall near Andhra Pradesh on October 28, triggering extremely heavy rainfall in parts of Odisha, West Bengal and other states. Here's full list of areas on alert on Oct 28, 29, 30:
The IMD issued a yellow alert in parts of West Bengal on October 28, 29 and 30.
Districts such as Purulia, Bankura, Jhargram, Purba Mednunupur, South 24 Parganas, Birbhum, Paschim Bardhaman, Hooghly and Nadia are on yellow alert on October 28.
On October 29, a yellow alert has been issued in all the districts of West Bengal, while on October 30, the IMD sounded an alert in parts of North Bengal – Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Jalpaiguri, Purba Bardhaman, Nadia, Coock Behar, Malda, Uttar Dinajpur and Birbhum.
Odisha
The landfall is likely to trigger severe weather, extremely heavy rainfall, and gusty winds across Odisha, particularly impacting its southern regions.
October 28: The IMD issued an orange alert in Malkangiri, Koraprayagarha, Gajaathi and Ganjam, while a yellow alert has been issued in Nabaranhapur, Kalahandi, Kandhamal, Khordha, Nayagarh, Puri, Mayurbhanj, Kendujhar and Kuttack among few other districts.
October 29: A red alert for extremely heavy rainfall has been issued in Malkangiri, Koraput, Rayagarha, Gajapthi and Ganjam. An orange alert has been issued in Nabaranhapur, Kalahandi, Nuapara, Balangir, Kandhamal, Khordha, Nayagarh and Puri. The remaining areas are on yellow alert.
October 30: Rainfall intensity in Odisha is likely to decrease. Only Sundargarh has been put on orange alert. Heavy rainfall is also likely in Deogarh, Jharsuguda, Sambalpur, Kendujhar, Mayurbhanj and Baleshwar.
Manorama Mohanty, Director of the Meteorological Centre in Bhubaneswar, told ANI that a 'Red Alert' has also been sounded for October 28 across five southern Odisha districts: Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, and Malkangiri, where isolated extremely heavy rainfall and wind speeds of 50 to 60 kmph, gusting up to 70 kmph, are anticipated.
"After landfall, it is likely to move close to Malkangiri district, but it will remain in Andhra Pradesh. Because of this, we are expecting extremely heavy rainfall... Landslides may also occur because we are expecting very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall, especially in the hilly areas," Mohanty added
Andhra Pradesh
Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is likely in North Andhra and Central Coastal districts on October 27 and 28, with isolated places likely to receive exceptionally heavy rainfall.
Kakinada, Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Konaseema and East Godavari districts, along with other parts of North Andhra, are expected to experience strong winds and heavy rainfall.
The intensity of rainfall is likely to be particularly high on October 27 and 28, officials told ANI.
Cyclone Arnab status update: When and where will it make landfall?
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in an update on Monday (October 26) that "deep depression intensified into Cyclonic Storm “Arnab”" over east-central and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal.
"It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm over west-central Bay of Bengal by midnight of today, the 26th October and into a very severe cyclonic storm over the same region on 27th October," the IMD said.
The weather department added that the system is very likely to move northwestwards and cross Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam as a very severe cyclonic storm by forenoon of October 28, 2026.

IMD weather today: ‘Red’ alert for heavy rains in Odisha, Kerala, Tamil Nadu as severe cyclonic storm nears Andhra IMD issues a red alert for Odisha and Kerala as a severe cyclonic storm nears the coast. Get the latest weather updates, rainfall warnings, and school closures. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall across several districts in Odisha and Kerala, while torrential downpours continue to disrupt normal life in Tamil Nadu. With severe waterlogging, localised flooding, and emergency rescues already underway in the southern states, authorities are bracing for further impact over the coming days. This comes as a depression over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into a deep depression and is rapidly moving towards the eastern coast, threatening to unleash destructive winds and massive storm surges. Severe cyclonic storm to hit Andhra coast; Odisha on red alert According to the IMD's latest bulletin, the deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam as a very severe cyclonic storm. The system is projected to make landfall by the forenoon of October 28, packing maximum sustained wind speeds of 115-125 kmph, gusting up to 140 kmph. With the projected landfall area situated roughly 300 kilometres from Gopalpur, the Odisha government has issued a red alert for five vulnerable southern districts—Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, and Malkangiri—for October 28. These areas are expected to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall, with isolated extremely heavy downpours exceeding 20 cm, accompanied by gusty surface winds reaching 60-70 kmph. As a precautionary measure, the chief minister has ordered the closure of all schools, colleges, and Anganwadi centres in these districts on October 28 and 29. Kerala issues red alert; schools, tourist spots shut In Keralam, heavy rains have severely disrupted normal life, causing waterlogging in numerous low-lying areas. In response, the IMD on Sunday issued a stringent red alert (indicating over 20 cm of rain in 24 hours) for Malappuram, Kozhikode, and Wayanad districts. Educational institutions and tourist destinations, including all adventure tourism and trekking locations, have been ordered shut in the red alert districts. The IMD also issued an orange alert for 10 other districts—including Thiruvananthapuram, Ernakulam, and Idukki—and a yellow alert for Kasaragod, forecasting strong winds at 40-50 kmph across the state. Tamil Nadu lashed by heavy rains Simultaneously, the northeast monsoon remains highly active over Tamil Nadu. Heavy to very heavy rain is likely in parts of the state on October 26 and 27, before scaling down to light or moderate showers over south Tamil Nadu on October 28. An IMD official clarified that while the Bay of Bengal cyclone is unlikely to directly affect Tamil Nadu, the state's ongoing rainfall is driven by a trough associated with a cyclonic circulation over the Southeast Arabian Sea and adjoining Lakshadweep. The state has already recorded massive downpours, with Burliyar receiving 25 cm of rain, and Devikapuram and Nedungunam recording 20 cm and 18 cm, respectively. The rains have triggered severe landslips in the ghat sections of the Nilgiris and Kodaikanal. Heavy machinery and sandbags have been deployed for restoration work, while the Coonnoor-Mettupalayam highway remains barred to traffic. Meanwhile, in Cuddalore district, disaster response teams safely rescued nine workers who were stranded on an isolated patch of land in a swollen river.
